content:
A Laredo man will spend the next 21 years in federal prison for supplying the fentanyl that killed another man in a 2023 hotel overdose, according to federal prosecutors.

U.S. District Judge Diana Saldana ordered Rene Antonio Melendez, 34, to serve 252 months in federal prison, to be followed by three years of supervised release, after he pleaded guilty on June 29 to conspiracy to distribute fentanyl resulting in death, Texas Border Business reported, citing the U.S. Attorney's Office for the Southern District of Texas.

The case traces back to March 11, 2023, when law enforcement responded to a Laredo hotel after receiving a report of an unresponsive man. The victim's friend told authorities the man had consumed a substance known as "White China" and stopped breathing. Investigators recovered a baggie containing fentanyl from the hotel room, and the medical examiner later determined the victim died from acute fentanyl toxicity.

According to prosecutors, the victim's friend had driven him to a location off San Bernardo Avenue to meet an unknown individual. Text messages revealed the victim had arranged to purchase $80 worth of drugs through Melendez, who directed him to that location. Cellphone records, witness interviews, and historical cell-site data established that Melendez was the individual who supplied the victim with fentanyl. Later that day, Melendez sent the victim a text message asking about the drugs; shortly afterward, the victim's friend called 911 to report the victim was not breathing.

Assistant U.S. Attorney Leslie Ann Cortez prosecuted the case. Melendez has been and will remain in custody pending transfer to a Federal Bureau of Prisons facility.

The prosecution was part of the Homeland Security Task Force initiative established by Executive Order 14159, a multi-agency partnership targeting cartels, transnational criminal organizations, and human smuggling and trafficking rings, with the U.S. Attorney's Office for the Southern District of Texas leading prosecutions in South Texas.

Sources: Texas Border Business, Oct. 21, 2026; U.S. Attorney's Office, Southern District of Texas.

title: Federal judge sentences Laredo man to 21 years in prison in fentanyl death case
